$comment: names.json: the names register of the scrapyard game (game id scrap-yard; ruling 14 in the lead's RULING.md; yard-design.md section 2 lists the names). Every invented proper noun is searched here BEFORE art or text is built on it. THIS IS AN ENGINEER'S CHECK, RECORDED AS SUCH: IT IS NOT LEGAL CLEARANCE. No trademark register (USPTO, EUIPO, UKIPO, WIPO Global Brand Database, CNIPA) was searched; the owner's own trade-mark search of at least the title is still required before release (yard-design.md 7.7, yard-policy.md 2). Filled on 2026-11-25 by the step labelled 'names'. Four checks per name: (a) a real company, brand or product of that name or one letter or one sound away, above all in metals, recycling, mining, electronics, cars, shipping and finance (UK Companies House search, web search, Bing exact-word results, the stores' publisher names); (b) a real exchange, index, port, town or region (web search, gazetteers met in results); (c) an app or game of that name on the stores (App Store search API, country US, 50 results; Google Play web search, US); (d) a name already used in this developer's four games, exact or one letter or one Soundex step away (grep of games/{pizza-empire,space-miner,night-market,high-office}/game.json, src/ui/{haul,merge,decree}/strings.ts, scripts/content/office/*.json and the three store files; plus scripts/content/build-space.py by hand for Orbit Haulers' sector and buyer names). Threshold used: an exact name of any real firm, product, app or game, or a word one letter or one sound from a real firm in the listed trades, a real town or region, or a name in the four games, fails; a common surname or given name shared only with unrelated small firms (builders, cafes) passes and is recorded. Verdicts: 'clear', 'changed' (with 'replacedBy'), 'new (replacement)' (with 'replaces'; it passed the same four checks). The specification is NOT edited here: the lead designer applies this register. Web queries contained only the candidate names and generic trade words. Method and scripts: notes/names.md in the shared notes folder. SECOND PASS (same day, step 'names'): the lead rejected first-pass replacements that a player cannot read or say ('Thwaiteby Lane', 'Skelderwick', 'Cradsworth', 'Hebblewick'). Every name a player sees most was chosen again from three short, plain candidates, each through the same four checks; the readability rule and the method are in 'secondPass'. Verdicts added: 'rejected (second pass ...)' on a first-pass replacement (with 'replacedBy' and 'rejectedBecause'), 'changed (second pass)' on a name the first pass had cleared, 'new (replacement, second pass)' with 'candidates'. On the specification's own names 'replacedBy' now gives the final name and 'firstPassReplacement' the one it replaces. The generated-name word lists are separate files beside this one (handle-words.json, company-words.json, crew-names.json, with name-filter.json and check-words.py). Still an engineer's check, not legal clearance. THIRD PASS (same day, step 'names'): ids. Every entry has an 'id' (lower-case dotted words; the first yard's camel-case ids are fixed by yard-stage1.md 5.1) that is stable for good: a renamed firm keeps its id. FORM CHOSEN: history stays in place as entries of the same id with "current": false; exactly one entry per id has "current": true, and that entry's 'name' is the name to show. 'byId' (id -> current name) is GENERATED from the entries by scripts/content/yard/build-ids.py; never edit it by hand. Test line: python3 -I scripts/content/yard/build-ids.py --check (exit 0 = byId agrees with the entries, one current entry per id, rival chips of at most 14 characters with none alike or one letter apart, merchant short form of at most 18); regenerate with python3 -I scripts/content/yard/build-ids.py. Rivals carry 'passTonnes' (a number, tonnes) on every entry of their id, and the current one a 'chip'; the merchant a 'short'; exchanges 'neverAbbreviate'. Data and code refer to names ONLY by id (D13, S21). 'summary.final' and 'summary.rivalLadder' are the second pass's record and are not updated: where they differ from byId, byId is right. Still an engineer's check, not legal clearance.

summary.readabilityRule: Second-pass rule (the lead, 2026-11-25): the player must be able to read and say the name. A twelve-year-old non-native speaker reads it aloud right the first time: one or two everyday morphemes of the trade or the landscape, at most three syllables a word, spelled as it sounds, no 'th' cluster, no '-thwaite', no '-wick' pile-ups, no silent 'gh'. A lane, a town or a port may share its name with small unrelated places or firms of no fame; what fails is one famous place, a brand, another game's title or setting, a word of this developer's four games, or a real exchange or port city.

secondPass.label: names (second pass)
secondPass.rule: Second-pass rule (the lead, 2026-11-25): the player must be able to read and say the name. A twelve-year-old non-native speaker reads it aloud right the first time: one or two everyday morphemes of the trade or the landscape, at most three syllables a word, spelled as it sounds, no 'th' cluster, no '-thwaite', no '-wick' pile-ups, no silent 'gh'. A lane, a town or a port may share its name with small unrelated places or firms of no fame; what fails is one famous place, a brand, another game's title or setting, a word of this developer's four games, or a real exchange or port city.
secondPass.method: For each place a player sees most (in the lead's order: home lane and yard, home town and vale, western exchange city, eastern country, exchange city and point, port, uplands site, eastern coast site, the two countries) three candidates were weighed; each candidate went through the first pass's four checks: (a) web search (WebSearch tool, the exact name in quotes with 'company OR game OR brand' and the like), UK Companies House search, App Store and Google Play publisher names; (b) Wikidata: the English Wikipedia page of that exact title and items labelled exactly so (the Wikipedia API itself refused this machine with a rate-limit page); (c) App Store search API (US) and Google Play search (US); (d) corpus.py over the four games. The firms: every first-pass replacement was read against the rule; those that fail it were replaced the same way. Bing (used by the first pass) was not used. The web search budget of the whole run (200 searches, shared with other engineers) ran out during this pass: Tolvan Motors, Clearmoor Glass, Cottle Demolition, Parfitt's Garage, Tap Street Plumbing and the rivals Brookmill, Tunney, Millbeck, Larkmoor, Stonebeck, Nordal and Tarnmoor have the company, store, Wikidata and four-games checks but NO web search; each entry says so. Queries held only the candidate names and generic words. Scripts: notes/names.md.

thirdPass.label: names (third pass)
thirdPass.method: Ids by the stage-1 specification (5.1) and in the same manner for the rest. The merchant: three candidates (and the specification's name) under the second-pass readability rule and the four checks. Rival chips: the distinctive word or two of each name, at most 14 characters; each chip read against the rule. Nine rival names failed it (Haddersby, Ashendry, Coralind by the second pass's own reasons; Morrance, Tervalen, Kestrane, Ondrell, Tarlevan, Vessendal as invented words with a stress the reader must guess) and were replaced from plain two-morpheme candidates. Checks run: UK Companies House search, App Store search API (US) and Google Play search (US), Wikidata (enwiki sitelink title and exact labels), corpus.py over the four games. WEB SEARCH WAS NOT RUN in this pass: the run's shared budget was already spent and the tool refused every query (Hookway, Tollbridge, Marlow, Bramley were tried). So the twelve second-pass names without a web search (Tolvan, Clearmoor, Cottle, Parfitt, Tap Street, Brookmill, Tunney, Millbeck, Larkmoor, Stonebeck, Nordal, Tarnmoor) and every third-pass name (Tollbridge, Bramley, Highfold, Pearlbay, Rookhill, Kilnfield, Hazelford, Wrenhill, Oakfold, Elmfield) still lack one; each entry says so. Bing was not used. Queries held only candidate names and generic words. Scripts: notes/names.md.
